Key Research Thinking Patterns: Two-Stage Hierarchical Filtering: A methodological strategy to enhance precision in noisy, web-scraped medical datasets by separating 'easy' from 'difficult' classification instances. (e.g., Implementing a ResNet-50 transfer learning model with SoftMax thresholding to achieve a 98.56% Positive Predictive Value for clean retinal fundus images, reducing false positives by two-thirds compared to single-stage models.)

Non-GAN Synthetic Data Augmentation: An approach to address class imbalance and data scarcity by algorithmically generating realistic training samples without the instability of Generative Adversarial Networks. (e.g., Extracting annotated lesion blobs from diseased retinal images and projecting them onto healthy images to improve classification accuracy by 7.4% in VGG16, ResNet-50, and Inception-v3 models.)

Joint Multi-Task Learning (J-Net): A framework that integrates semantic segmentation and image classification into a single unified architecture to leverage shared feature representations for small datasets. (e.g., Combining U-Net for lesion segmentation with a binary classifier to outperform independent single-task models on skin cancer datasets with limited training samples of 200-1200 images.)

Hybrid Morphological-Deep Learning: A strategy to enhance model stability and interpretability on imbalanced medical data by integrating mathematical morphology operations with deep neural networks. (e.g., Developing a Morphological-Convolutional Neural Network (MCNN) trained with Extreme Learning Machine and Random Forest to achieve an AUC of 0.704 for glaucoma detection on the ORIGA dataset, demonstrating better balanced accuracy than standard CNNs trained from scratch.)
Summary Description: Sanjana Mudduluru is a researcher specializing in Medical Imaging Informatics and Computer-Aided Diagnosis, with a primary focus on ophthalmology and dermatology. Her work addresses critical challenges in deep learning for healthcare, specifically data scarcity, class imbalance, and the quality of web-scraped datasets. Key technical contributions include the development of a two-stage ResNet-50 system for automated retinal image quality control, a non-GAN algorithm for synthetic retinal fundus generation via lesion projection, and a joint U-Net-based architecture (J-Net) for simultaneous segmentation and classification. Additionally, she explores hybrid models integrating mathematical morphology with CNNs (MCNN) to improve stability on small, imbalanced datasets. Her research aims to enhance the reliability and accuracy of clinical decision support systems by creating robust, data-efficient deep learning frameworks for diagnosing conditions such as glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and skin cancer.
